chain_findings.description: IAM privilege escalation via policy attachment. A user or role has iam:AttachUserPolicy, iam:AttachRolePolicy, or iam:AttachGroupPolicy permission — enabling them to attach an admin-grade managed policy to any principal they can reach, including themselves. This is a single-API-call escalation path documented in Rhino Security's CloudGoat and Bishop Fox's IAM Vulnerable. The escalation is latent: the principal currently has low privileges, but one API call (AttachUserPolicy) grants full admin. No runtime exploit is required — the configuration alone enables the path. Threshold of 1: AttachUserPolicy alone is sufficient for escalation. The inline-policy member is an amplifier — if the account also has roles with inline policies (shadow permissions), the escalation target surface is broader than managed-policy auditing reveals.

near_miss_chains.description: Principal can simulate any other principal's permissions (iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy) AND has an escalation vector. SimulatePrincipalPolicy is the most efficient target selection tool — one API call tells the attacker exactly what each potential victim can do. Combined with credential manipulation or policy attachment, this enables programmatic identification of the highest-value target before executing the escalation.

Principal can enumerate IAM principals AND read their policies AND has a privilege escalation vector. This enables surgical selection of the highest-privilege target for escalation rather than blind exploitation. The attacker identifies the programmatic-only service account with admin permissions and no MFA, creates console access for it, and logs in with full privileges.

Unrestricted iam:AttachUserPolicy privilege escalation. A user has iam:AttachUserPolicy on self (ATTACHUSERPOLICY.001) AND the grant lacks an iam:PolicyARN condition (NOCONDITION.001). Together this means the principal can attach any of AWS's 1,000+ managed policies — including AdministratorAccess — to itself with a single API call. Unlike AddUserToGroup (which requires a pre-existing privileged group), AttachUserPolicy is self-sufficient: AWS managed policies are the escalation payload and they are always available. Threshold 2: both must fire to confirm the path is unrestricted. A condition-restricted AttachUserPolicy (partial case) fires only the capability control, not this chain.
